metadata.conclusion_map: PBPS: literal augmentation law is invariant under R(x,y)=(x,2x-y), and R is involutive. Concentration background: the product Gaussian integral is unchanged by rotation, enabling conditional Stein/covariance calculation. Only coordinate-law invariance is shared; neither conclusion is a PBPS process-invariance theorem or Gaussian LSI/T2 certificate.
metadata.failure_boundary: Rotating an arbitrary mu with a Gaussian does not preserve mu product gamma: at theta=pi/2 a non-Gaussian or noncentered mu is swapped with gamma. PBPS avoids that by fixing the arbitrary input. Gaussian reflection and rotation are different maps; reflection involutivity is not a generic rotation conclusion. Identically distributed centered anisotropic Gaussian copies may retain rotation invariance, but isotropic sharp coefficient1/2 in the given metric cannot be inferred. No PBPS reflection theorem implies the sharp concentration bound, nonexplosion, hypocoercivity, actual algorithm or query costs. No certified functor/equivalence or solid Lean dependency is claimed.
metadata.hypothesis_map: Common: actual measurable maps and law-preservation identity. PBPS: nu=mu product stdGaussian, arbitrary probability mu, S(x,z)=(x,-z), Phi(x,z)=(x,x+sqrt(eta)z), eta>0. Concentration background: nu=stdGaussian product itself, Phi=id and R=S=T_theta, T_theta(x,z)=(cos(theta)x+sin(theta)z,-sin(theta)x+cos(theta)z); both inputs Gaussian, centered and with identical covariance. The actual source standard-Gaussian instance has identity covariance in the Hilbert metric; the sharp numerical coefficient requires a separate covariance-scale/concentration calibration and does not follow from product-rotation law invariance alone.
metadata.mechanism: Preserve an underlying centered Gaussian law by an appropriate linear symmetry, then transport the symmetry through an actual measurable generative map. PBPS flips the noise while fixing the arbitrary input; the authored SPHMC concentration background rotates two independent identically distributed centered Gaussian copies before conditional Stein. Measure preservation permits changing integration coordinates. This does not identify the algorithms or their convergence guarantees.
